title: edit.redo
description: Redoes the entry on top of OpenTune's redo history (PROTOCOL.md section 15.3). Without force, expectedUndoId is required and must name that entry, else the call fails with UNDO_CONFLICT(top_mismatch). With force true the server applies the top entry whatever it is and neither parses nor checks expectedUndoId, which may be left out; clients set force only when the end user explicitly asked to redo a change that was not made through the client. An empty history gives UNDO_CONFLICT(history_empty), also with force; a clip split, merge or delete gives UNSUPPORTED(undo_unsafe_build), also with force. An entry is possibly stale (possiblyStale in edit.getHistory) when a track was deleted after it was recorded and no call with force has applied it since. Without force, a possibly stale entry recorded through this API gives UNDO_CONFLICT(stale_entry); such an entry is possibly stale only when a track it addresses has moved or was removed since, so an entry recorded through this API whose tracks did not move is applied as usual, without a warning. Without force, a possibly stale entry recorded in the UI, which the server cannot inspect, is applied with the warning UNDO_ENTRY_POSSIBLY_STALE; with force, a possibly stale entry is applied without that warning. A call with force that applies an entry clears its possiblyStale, because the end user has confirmed the entry. Changes without an undo entry are never taken back: an entry recorded through this API puts back only the aspects of a content that its own change touched, and no longer those that a later change without an undo entry changed; such a change also clears the redo history (section 15.3 rule 9). A step that changes nothing still succeeds, with noOp true and the warning UNDO_NO_EFFECT; as in OpenTune, the step is used up and the project is marked as changed. entry is the applied entry as it is after the step: an entry that had no undoId has the one the server assigned now (section 15.3 rule 8), and after a call with force possiblyStale is false. revisionDiff and changes describe the effect, from snapshots taken before and after the step; a content whose notes or pitch curve changed is listed as an entry of entity content with the field revision. Like the UI, the server then refreshes derived state; work this queues is reported in sideEffects. The step creates no undo entry of its own (undo reason ui_parity); its revert recipe is edit.undo with the entry's undoId and without force, so that, sent unchanged, it takes back exactly this step, also after a step applied with force.

expectedUndoId.description: The undoId of the entry the client expects on top of the history. Required, and checked, unless force is true; with force true the server ignores it, whatever its value.

undo.description: The step's own undo descriptor: no undo entry (reason ui_parity), and edit.undo with the applied entry's undoId as revert recipe. The recipe's params hold only expectedUndoId: they never carry force (PROTOCOL.md section 15.3 rule 8).
